_meta.purpose: Committed offline source of DATED, REAL named-festival occurrences that feed travel_pulse_calendar_events -> the R33 event spotlight (demand-onepager) and Discover 'event approaching' lens. Config-only literals; NO LLM-generated rows. Every entry is a documented annual/fixed-date festival from the official calendars named in docs/planning/TRAILHEAD_ANCHOR_SOURCE_REGISTRY_v1.md.
_meta.honesty: crowdImpact / priceImpact / crowdImpactPercent are deliberately OMITTED (null in the DB) — a guessed surge metric is exactly the class §13 forbids; the R33 consumers read only eventName/startDate/endDate, so a bare dated row is fully honest.

attribution.kyoto_city_tourism: Kyoto City Tourism Association / Kyoto City Official Events calendar (kyoto.travel) — annual matsuri are fixed-date recurring events.
attribution.edinburgh_festivals: VisitScotland / Forever Edinburgh + festival operators — fixed-date national/city observances only; the variable-date August festivals (Fringe/EIF/Tattoo) are intentionally NOT hardcoded here (their dates are published per-year and must not be guessed — see report).
attribution.nager_date: date.nager.at public-holiday API — added at ingest time by the live-fetch path (⚑ Replit), MIT-licensed open data.

_meta.recurrence: Exactly one of: fixedDate {month,day,durationDays?} (annual on that calendar day), dateRange {startMonth,startDay,endMonth,endDay} (annual window), or dates [YYYY-MM-DD...] (year-specific explicit).

festivals.description: Seasonal bean-throwing rites at Yoshida, Yasaka and other Kyoto shrines marking the start of spring.
One of Kyoto's three great festivals; Heian-costumed procession from the Imperial Palace to the Kamo shrines.
Yasaka Shrine's month-long July festival, Kyoto's largest; float displays and street events across central Kyoto.
The main float procession of Gion Matsuri through central Kyoto.
The second float procession of Gion Matsuri.
Giant bonfire characters lit on five Kyoto mountainsides to send off ancestral spirits at the close of Obon.
The 'Festival of the Ages'; a historical costume procession from the Imperial Palace to Heian Shrine.
Nighttime torch procession at Yuki Shrine in the northern Kurama district.
Scotland-wide celebration of the poet Robert Burns, widely observed across Edinburgh.
Scotland's national day, marked with events across Edinburgh.
Edinburgh's flagship New Year celebration spanning 31 December into 1 January.
